models.label: wav2vec2-base phoneme CTC — INT8 (slow on WebGPU, keep for WASM)
models.notes: wav2vec2-base (94.4M params, bookbot/wav2vec2-ljspeech-gruut) fine-tuned for IPA phoneme CTC output. Dynamic INT8 quantization applied to MatMul/Gemm ops only — the 7-layer conv feature extractor and the positional conv embedding stayed FP32 because their weight-norm reparameterization (a Mul feeding Conv) isn't a quantizer-recognized constant initializer. FP32 source was 377.8MB; this build is 121.9MB (32%). MEASURED 2026-08-01, real iPad, WebGPU: 572ms mean per utterance — 4.9x SLOWER than the FP16 build of the identical checkpoint. Do not ship this on the WebGPU path. Kept because INT8 kernels are mature on WASM/CPU and it is very likely still the right choice for the WASM fallback path — that comparison has not been run on-device yet.

models.label: wav2vec2-base phoneme CTC — FP16 (default, WebGPU winner)
models.notes: Same checkpoint, weights/activations cast to FP16 (onnxconverter-common float16.convert_float_to_float16, keep_io_types=True so input_values/logits stay FP32 — no harness changes needed). MEASURED 2026-08-01, real iPad, WebGPU, 20 reps post-warmup: 116.75ms mean / 117ms median / 121ms p95, range 113-121ms. PASSES the 300ms budget with 2.6x headroom, and is 4.9x faster than the INT8 build of the identical checkpoint (572ms). That confirms the hypothesis this file was built to test: INT8 quantization was actively hurting on WebGPU, not helping — INT8 kernel paths are mature on WASM/CPU but thin on current WebGPU backends. Verified correct (not just fast) against real speech from this repo's own voice pack before shipping, same as the INT8 build.
